Built-in steps for composing a run

Source: R/doc-steps.R
gr_step.Rd

gr_step() builds one stage of a run as a step: a function of (input, ctx) that ingests, segments or reads. gr_step_retrieve() builds a step that ranks the chunks against the question and keeps the best, as the retrieve reader does, without the answer request. The settings are checked when the step is built, by the spec constructors (gr_ingest_spec(), gr_segment_spec(), gr_read_spec()), so a misspelt or out-of-range setting fails there and not on the hundredth run of a benchmark.

Usage

gr_step(kind = c("ingest", "segment", "read"), ..., name = NULL)

gr_step_retrieve(top_k = 6L, ..., name = NULL)

Arguments

kind

"ingest", "segment" or "read".

...

Settings for the stage's spec constructor: gr_ingest_spec() for "ingest", gr_segment_spec() for "segment", gr_read_spec() for "read" (reader = "stuff", say). For gr_step_retrieve(), the other ranking settings of gr_read_spec(): min_score, mmr, fusion, rrf_k, lexical_blend, bm25_k1, bm25_b.

name

The step's name; defaults to kind, or "retrieve".

top_k

How many chunks to keep, as in gr_read_spec().

Value

A function of (input, ctx) with class c("gr_step", "hr_step", "function").

Details

A step uses ctx$client for its requests and records them on ctx$trace, which is what hr_benchmark() gives an arm's run function: inside an hr_arm() every request a step makes is counted, held to the benchmark's limits and sent at the run's draw. Outside a benchmark, pass a list such as list(client = cl, trace = gr_trace()).

Steps pass a list along. The first step takes the item (gr_qa_reference() items are lists with question and document); "ingest" adds doc, "segment" adds chunks (ingesting document first when there is no doc), and gr_step_retrieve() replaces chunks with the chunks it kept, best first, with their scores in a score column. "read" reads chunks (segmenting first when there are none) and returns the gr_answer. hr_chain() runs steps in order as one arm; by hand, the same is a fold: Reduce(function(x, step) step(x, ctx), steps, item).

Each step is an hr_step() with class gr_step added and the attributes kind and spec, which print() shows. Its settings are checked against the stage's schema: gr_ingest_spec()'s, gr_segment_spec()'s or gr_read_spec()'s for gr_step(), and for gr_step_retrieve() the ranking settings top_k, min_score, mmr, fusion, rrf_k, lexical_blend, bm25_k1 and bm25_b. Any other setting passed to gr_step_retrieve() reaches gr_read_spec() as it is. A step declares what it takes and returns, which hr_chain() checks: ingest takes a document and returns a doc, segment takes a doc and returns chunks, retrieve takes and returns chunks, and read takes chunks and returns the answer.

These steps take no skill (hr_skill()): their requests are built by the stage, not sent through ctx$call(), so a skill would not reach them. Passing skill is an error of class hr_bad_skill.

See also

hr_chain(), which runs steps as one arm; hr_step() for a step of your own; gr_arm() for a whole recipe as one arm.

Other reading functions: gr_answer, gr_check_reader(), gr_methods_text(), gr_read(), gr_read_spec(), gr_reader_signature(), gr_readers(), gr_register_reader(), is_not_found(), new_answer()

Examples

cl <- gr_mock_client(function(m, p) "Revenue was 45.2 million dollars.")
ctx <- list(client = cl, trace = gr_trace())
steps <- list(gr_step("segment", method = "paragraph", max_tokens = 120),
              gr_step_retrieve(top_k = 2),
              gr_step("read", reader = "stuff"))
item <- list(question = "What was revenue?", document = gr_example())
ans <- Reduce(function(x, step) step(x, ctx), steps, item)
#> Using cached ingestion for this document + settings.
#> Segmenting with 'paragraph' (cap 120 tokens, overlap 0).
#> Reading with 'stuff' (all|1|none) over 2 chunk(s).
ans$chunks_used
#> [1] 2 6

# The same steps as an arm a benchmark can run.
arm <- hr_chain(segment = steps[[1]], retrieve = steps[[2]], read = steps[[3]],
                name = "segment-rank-read")
steps[[2]]
#> <gr_step> retrieve (retrieve): top_k=2
